name: Reverse EZ-Bar Curl
description: The reverse EZ-bar curl uses an overhand (pronated) grip on an EZ-curl bar to target the brachioradialis and brachialis rather than the biceps brachii, which is in a mechanically disadvantaged position in pronation. The EZ-bar's angle reduces wrist stress compared to a straight bar reverse curl. This exercise builds the forearm and arm thickness from the outside and helps balance pulling strength.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding an EZ-bar with a pronated (overhand) grip at the outer grip positions. Arms extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Use the outer grip on the EZ-bar for the most comfortable wrist angle. Use lighter weight than underhand curls.
steps: Step 1: Curl the EZ-bar upward with a pronated grip.
Step 2: Keep the elbows at the sides and curl to maximum elbow flexion.
Step 3: Lower slowly back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Rotating to a neutral grip during the curl
Excessive wrist extension at the bottom
safety_considerations: Avoid wrist hyperextension — keep wrists straight throughout
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension to maximum elbow flexion.
coaching_cues: Pronated grip stays all the way
